title: 3DG: A Framework for Using Generative AI for Handling Sparse Learner Performance Data From Intelligent Tutoring Systems
venue: LAK'24: International Workshop on Generative AI for Learning Analytics (GenAI-LA)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of sparse learner performance data in intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs), where missing quiz scores, attempts, and related interaction data can weaken learner modeling, knowledge tracing, and performance prediction. The authors argue that sparsity is especially problematic because it can bias downstream analysis and limit the usefulness of ITS learner models.

To tackle this, the paper proposes 3DG (3-Dimensions, Densification, and Generation), a framework that first represents ITS interaction data as a three-dimensional tensor over learners, questions, and attempts. The framework then uses tensor factorization for data imputation and generative models for data augmentation. Two generative approaches are compared: GAN and GPT-4. The GPT approach is supported by mixed prompts and chain-of-thought prompting, while GAN uses a standard generator-discriminator setup.

The framework is demonstrated on an AutoTutor reading comprehension dataset from the Center for the Study of Adult Literacy (CSAL), involving 118 adult participants in the United States. The paper reports that tensor completion can effectively fill missing values and that GAN produced more reliable simulated data than GPT-4 in this setting, with narrower and more consistent parameter distributions. The authors conclude that generative models, especially GANs, can help address data sparsity in ITSs, while noting that GPT-4 currently performs less well for numerical simulation tasks and that future work should examine hybrid GAN-GPT approaches and robustness to different sparsity levels.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed workshop/framework paper with a clear applied method and real dataset, but it is not an experimental evaluation of student outcomes. Evidence is methodological and comparative in nature rather than a rigorous causal study.
impact_tier_rationale: The work suggests a potentially useful tooling advance for handling sparse ITS logs, but it reports no direct K-12 learning gains or effect sizes. Impact is therefore plausible but unclear and indirect.

interventions.use_case: Methods paper proposing a framework to impute and augment sparse learner performance data drawn from an AutoTutor intelligent tutoring lesson (reading comprehension) using tensor factorization plus generative models.
Uses GPT-4 as a generative model to simulate learner performance sequences from sparse ITS data, comparing its outputs against GAN-generated simulations.
Generative AI for simulation and data augmentation of sparse educational performance data, specifically comparing GAN and GPT-4 for generating synthetic learner-attempt traces.

finding.finding_summary: The paper uses an AutoTutor reading-comprehension lesson from CSAL (n=118) as the source data, so the substantive educational domain is literacy. However, the study does not evaluate learner reading gains; it evaluates whether tensor completion and generative models can reconstruct/simulate sparse reading-performance traces. No student-achievement effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Reading-comprehension performance traces from AutoTutor (binary correct/incorrect attempts; simulated parameter distributions for learner ability and learning rate)

finding.finding_summary: The framework is presented as improving the practicality of analysis and modeling in ITS by imputing missing values and generating scalable synthetic datasets from sparse learner-performance data. The paper reports that the original dataset had 80%–85% sparsity and that tensor completion successfully densified it, but it does not provide a formal efficiency effect size.
finding.measure: Ability to impute missing values and generate scalable simulated learner-performance data from sparse ITS logs
